text.title: Ads Attribution Models Failure Modes
text.summary: 12 antipatterns observed in real deployments of Ads Attribution Models — platform sums as truth, no incrementality tests, definition drift, raw cross-platform comparison, short or disturbed incrementality tests, last-click only, ignored view-through, and four LLM-agent gotchas (narrating noise, unlabeled tables, timezone mixing, point estimates without CIs). Each pairs symptom + sourced root-cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Team sums Meta + Google + LinkedIn self-reports; total exceeds actual sales by 40%; budgets misallocated.
antipattern.fix: Set warehouse as truth; treat platform reports as inputs; rebuild reconciliation pipeline.

antipattern.symptom: Attribution model credits brand 30%; geo-holdout shows brand drives 0% incremental; budget wasted for 12 months.
antipattern.fix: Run quarterly geo-holdout per major channel; rebalance budget on true lift.

antipattern.symptom: Conversion window changed mid-quarter; apparent 25% variance triggers false alarm.
antipattern.fix: Freeze definitions quarterly; document change windows; communicate to reviewers.

antipattern.symptom: Comparing platform-reported conversions directly across channels to determine which channel is "winning."
antipattern.root-cause: Platform totals are not deduplicated. A user clicking both Meta and Google appears in both reports as a unique conversion. The comparison is meaningless without a unified view.
antipattern.fix: Compare channels only in the GA4 or warehouse-deduped view (deduped-view-for-cross-channel rule); keep platform numbers for in-platform optimization.

antipattern.symptom: Running an incrementality test for less than 2 weeks or adjusting budgets during the test.
antipattern.root-cause: Insufficient runtime produces statistically noisy results. Mid-test budget changes alter the treatment condition and make the holdout comparison invalid.
antipattern.fix: Pre-register a 4-week minimum and freeze budgets and targeting for the whole window (incrementality-four-weeks-frozen rule); restart the test if either is broken.

antipattern.symptom: Trusting platform-reported totals for cross-channel budget decisions.
antipattern.root-cause: Platform totals are over-counted by 20-40% due to cross-channel overlap. Decisions based on them systematically overspend on channels that appear more efficient than they are.
antipattern.fix: Route every budget decision through the deduped source of truth and the three-numbers-per-channel variance check.

antipattern.symptom: Using last-click as the sole attribution model for a multi-touch journey.
antipattern.root-cause: Last-click assigns zero credit to all upper-funnel touchpoints, leading to systematic under-investment in awareness and consideration channels.
antipattern.fix: Select the model by sales cycle and conversion volume (model-by-sales-cycle rule); keep last-click only as a secondary comparison view.

antipattern.root-cause: Display and video channels drive brand recall that appears as direct traffic. Excluding view-through undervalues awareness spend.
antipattern.fix: Report view-through separately with its window labeled; validate awareness channels with geo-holdout rather than dropping them.

antipattern.symptom: Agent explains small variances (under 15%) with elaborate narratives before a minimum-variance threshold is met.
antipattern.root-cause: Small variances are noise from lookback window differences, timezone offsets, and sampling. Narratives on noise mislead decision-makers.
antipattern.fix: Report sub-15% variance as "within noise" with no narrative; investigate and narrate only above the threshold (variance-threshold-15 rule).

antipattern.symptom: Agent presents platform-reported and GA4-modeled numbers side-by-side as comparable values without labeling the model and window for each.

root-cause.source: Meta / Google Ads / GA4 attribution settings docs

antipattern.root-cause: They use different lookback windows and deduplication logic. An unlabeled table implies comparability where none exists.
antipattern.fix: Every column carries model + window in its header (document-platform-defaults rule); tables without labels are rejected at review.

antipattern.symptom: Agent computes a single "today" number using GA4 property timezone and Google Ads account timezone interchangeably.
antipattern.root-cause: GA4 uses property timezone; Google Ads uses account timezone. These can differ by hours and produce off-by-one date errors in daily reports.
antipattern.fix: Normalize every source to one reporting timezone in the pipeline before any daily rollup; record the source timezone per row.

antipattern.symptom: Agent reports data-driven attribution point estimates without confidence intervals or sample-size caveats.
antipattern.root-cause: Data-driven models have uncertainty that grows with low conversion volume. Point estimates without CIs create false precision and overconfident recommendations.
antipattern.fix: Attach conversion volume per channel and a confidence interval or "insufficient volume" flag to every data-driven share; below 50 conversions/channel/month, fall back to a rule-based model.
